title: AERO9500 Final Report (Part 2)
overview: Design a simple preliminary space mission benefiting Australia and identify main elements of its space segment, demonstrating understanding of space segment systems (launch, orbits etc.) using mission design software plus hand calculations.
deliverables: Technical report as single PDF including/referencing relevant screenshots
All relevant STK or PIGI design files (in report or appendix)

format.length: 20 pages max for core part - excludes title page, table of contents, references, etc.
format.structure: Must include sections: Executive summary; Introduction - mission overview and rationale; Main body [launch, orbit, ground stations, coverage, mission operation and end-of-life]; Conclusion; Bibliography
format.other: Engineering technical report style - clear, effective, correct grammar and spelling. Figures and tables fully and correctly labelled with number, title and reference if needed. All non-original text/diagrams/ideas cited and referenced; Wikipedia not acceptable as source. Plagiarism check.

requirements.text: Define spacecraft's primary mission - must benefit Australia, keep concept simple (examples: bushfire tracking/alert, weather satellite, internet/communication, Earth observation for city planning/real estate).
State whether one or multiple spacecraft will be used.
Specify launch location and launch vehicle.
Specify orbit type, its characteristics and orbital elements.
Determine if any orbital maneuvers are required and detail them.
Identify which ground control facilities will be used and how often spacecraft can communicate with ground control, including coverage analysis.
Define mission duration and plans for End-of-Life (EOL).

Use mission design software of choice (STK industry-standard, PIGI from Saber Astronautics requires competition registration for license, or other e.g. flightclub only after contacting Naomi) to complete design, supplemented with hand calculations as needed.
Include in main body all space segment aspects: launch, orbit, ground stations, coverage, mission operation and end-of-life.
